pronunciation.title: Say it right from day one

rules.explain: a=AH, e=EH, i=EE, o=OH, u=OO. Always. So CASA is KAH-sah.

rules.rule: H is silent, J sounds like H
rules.explain: HOLA is OH-lah (no H sound). J in JUEVES sounds like English H: HWEH-vehs.
Ñ is like NY in canyon: NIÑO = NEEN-yoh. LL and Y sound like Y in yes.
Tap your tongue once for R. PERRO (dog) rolls longer than PERO (but).
Most words stress the middle: HOLA = OH-lah, GRACIAS = GRAH-syahs. An accent mark (á) forces stress there.

alphabet.title: The Uzbek alphabet (Latin): 32 letters
alphabet.explain: Uzbek's official Latin alphabet has 32 letters. The apostrophe does real work: it marks the deep throat sounds q and g (to'rt, beg'ona). Every syllable is open — a consonant plus a vowel — so words sound even and regular.

counting.title: Counting in Uzbek: 0 to 15
counting.explain: Eleven and up is o'n (ten) + the number: o'n bir, o'n ikki, o'n uch.
rules: Vowel harmony: words built from back vowels (a o u) take back-vowel endings; front vowels (e i) take front ones.
The apostrophe letters (q, g, x, h) are deep throat sounds — friends of Arabic qāf.
There is no c, no w and no y: those letters simply do not exist in the Uzbek Latin alphabet.
